x: Stephen WHITE (Surrey)
Main points scorers have been John Kelly, Tony Brooks and Philip Gee - all first year Juniors, and Stevie White who is only a first year Youth and one of the most promising young athletes we have.
Our leading points scorer in the Youths section was Steve White who won the two sprints and the Long Jump. He was another who had competed in the LAC meeting..
It is obvious that with a little extra training, John, Eric Wickens, Geoff Shaw and Steve White will end up with performances equalling those of last years Junior team.
Earlier, Tony Brooks had failed to get through his heat although clocking 10.6 and Steve White ran his best of 10.8 in the Youth semi-final.

Amongst the Youths Arnold Bent and Steve White stand supreme. With sprinter David Rees, John and Bob Hamilton over the 'half' and 'quarter' and new members Michael and Trevor Day and John Crockford over the longer distances, we have the makings of a first class Youth team.

Steve White really impressed in this meeting notching up a 10.5 hundred and a 23.4 furlong - times which speak for themselves. David Wilkinson scored his first points for us in a club match, winning the Javelin by seven feet and also scoring in the Junior match.
Steve White reached 19'6½" on the Thursday night to place second in the Long Jump and then on Saturday loped to easy wins in the heat and final of the 100 yards.

Features of the afternoon were Jim Vivian's floating 'quarter' in 50.9, John Thresher's front running from gun to tape in 4:11.8, Stevie White's 10.5 win in the 100yds Junior (he is only a youth) and the necessity to run three heats in the Boys 100yds.

Bill Curtin ran his best race yet - 2:05.0 for the 880y - in his heat, a time that was not beaten even in the final, but here Bill was badly boxed in and could only get up to 5th with 2:09.4. Arnold Bent was 6th in the High Jump with 5'8 and Steve White was a member of the winning London Relay Team.
Amongst the Juniors Tony Brooks scored a large percentage of our points and Steve White, only a Youth, took the two 'A' sprints by impressive margins.

… start to the season due to glandular fever Jim Vivian and Chris Martin had both better look out for the fast improving Steve White, who has recorded times over the longer sprint that Jim and Chris have yet to beat this year.…

In the sprints, Steve White (17) pushed international Dave Dear all the way in the 'A' 100 and coasted to an easy victory in the 'B' 220. A fine run by John Dear in the steeplechase and a promising 440 by Jim Vivian on the last leg of the medly relay were also noteworthy, but the finest performance…

Despite a windy and rain swept afternoon, some very good performances were set up; the most notable being Steve White's 200 metres run of 22.1 which is the fastest time this year by a British junior over the distance.

The outstanding performers at this year's championships were Steve White, Chris Martin and Nick Head. The first two chalked up sprint trebles in the Junior & Senior grades respectively, and the latter repeated his "pinta" treble of last year shot/discus/javelin.

Star of the Championships was undoubtedly Steve White who pulled off an excellent treble in the Junior 100, 220 and long jump events. His 22'-4" in the latter was only 1" inferior to that of the senior winner, international John Howell.

Most outstanding were Steve White in the 200 metres and Arnold Bent in the High Jump and Bill Curtin winning the 800 metres once again. Steve looked terrific, and who can say where this fellow will advance in the world of sprinting.
(Photo by Ed Lacey) Steve White wins the Surrey Co Junior 100 yards from Sinclair(Surrey AC). Later. he clinched a notable treble by taking the Junior 220 yards and long-jump titles.

Only a first year junior and showing all the class of an international, Steve White hit the straight yards up on Dave Williams of Notts A.C. and only in the last few yards did Williams pull past to win; leaving Steve second with a Club Junior Record.

It is doubtful whether anyone expected us to do well as we were without Steve White on this occasion. Dave Rees got us away to a fine start handing over with a lead to Mick Franks who increased this with great power and completed a great batton change with Arnold Bent who ran superbly to give John H…

Steve White has been in great form this season,winning the London Schools 200 metres and placing 3rd in the English Championships 220 yards with 22.2 - a great prospect who will probably find his metier in the 440 yards.
Steve White, our star sprinter, ran in the 220 yards winning his heat in 22.2 seconds. In the final he was drawn in Lane 6, but ran the bend of his life to lead by about 2 yards into the straight.
Jim Vivian with a 21.8 yards remains top dog, but close behind is first year junior, Steve White, 22.1. Chris Martin with 22.2 fills third place.

Steve White 10.4 We have been fortunate in being allowed the use of a large room at a local boys Club in Southwark and during the past weeks the boys have been busy cleaning and painting it to our own requirements putting up pictures of favorite athletes (excellent photographs kindly given to us by Ed Lacy).
400 metres youths 1.Steve White 53.0

Steve White, Bill Curtin, Martin Bloice, Richard Langley, Arnold Bentt, Lee Sullivan and Peter Carton are just a few of the names that come to mind and (dare we hope?) seem to have overcome the difficult periods which face all youngsters who try to take their athletics seriously.
Steve White 21.9 (record)

Potentially two of our strongest events, but with Jim Vivian plagued by injury, Steve White sitting his "A" levels and John Mitchell with heavy university commitments in the early season, it hasn't usually worked out that way.
Our best performances came from John Thresher and Geoff North in the 1500, Derek Glendinning and Bob Couillault in the Triple Jump and our "B" string sprinters Steve White and Chris Martin.
Otherwise, the most impressive athlete on view was Steve White, who managed a personal best 100 metres in the conditions, as well as completing his junior triple with the 200 and 400 as well.
Despite our own Steve White running the last leg for Tulse Hill School, Belgrave won the 4 X 110 yards Junior relay title by a fifth of a second in 44.8.
Britain's fastest Junior sprinter of 1969, Belgravian Steve White, wins the Southern 200 metres in 21.8. He later recorded the same time in the A.A.A.

…race, he did in that one---even though he failed to win he deserved every bit of praise for such a distinguished effort.Steve White's seemingly effortless fastest junior 200 metres of the year---what a superb advertisement he is for our sport and Club.…
TULSE HILL---Star of the London Schools Championships was Steve White who, on the fast Crystal Palace track, set a remarkable 21.7 to head the 1969 National Junior rankings.

Title holders Steve White (21.7) and Lee Sullivan (21'-9½") had no difficulty in holding on to their number one positions in the Senior ranks, but Arnold Bent relinquished his high jump title to rival Alexander who won on the count back---both clearing 5'-9¾".
Steve White confirmed his liking for the tartan surfacing by sweeping to another 200 metres victory in 21.8 seconds, just a tenth outside his previous best but a tenth better than the previous A.A.A.
In the Junior 4X100metres relay we were without the services of Steve White who was assisting his school, Tulse Hill. We were last in our heat with a poor 45.1 seconds.

Producing his usual blazing burst round the turn, Steve White led the finalists into the straight and looked set to win his first AAA Championship, but he faded badly down the straight and Griffith swept past to take the title by a tenth in 21.7.
Probably our strongest events on paper with Steve White, Jim Vivian, John Mitchell and Chris Martin and able assistance from Aris Sapountzoglou, Tony and Cliff Brooks.
Steve White scored a sprint double (10.5 y/22.5y) while Arnold Bentt leapt a season's best 22'-1¼" to finish 2nd in the long jump and followed up with a below par high jump (5'-7") for 6th.
:(Ron Linstead) A classic shot of classic styles shows Steve White (left) winning from Bruno Hafner in the final of the Club Championship 100 metres.

Nevertheless, we are hardly short of class with Steve White , already a county champion at 200 metres, and Jim Vivian available. We have annexed a fine sprinter from Switzerland in Bruno Hafner, who has already given Steve a couple of close races.

Our outstanding performers were Steve White, winner of the 'B'100 metres, 2nd in the 'A'200 metres and a member of both relay teams; Jim Vivian, 4th in the 'A' 100 metres, 1st in the 'B'200 metres and a member of the winning sprint relay team; John Thresher and Bob Smith, 2nd respectively in the 'A'…

The man whom Martin eyed with most interest was another former Youth star, now fulfilling the promise he always showed, Steve White. Steve showed all the majesty of a true champion as he smoothly powered his way to the Senior 200 title; in this his first year too.

The "doubles" went to Steve White (100/200), Mel Ford (400/800) and Glyn Ratcliffe (Shot/Discus) - all in good form. Martin Bloice, our new Surrey County Youth Champion, had no need to repeat his 51.3 of the previous week in winning the Junior 400 - but he was chased hard by Elliott and Langley.

Our winners were Bruno Hafner ('B' 100 metres), Lionel Mann ('B' 5000 metres), Alan Black ('B' steeplechase), Charlie Gillett ('B' 400 metres hurdles), Arnold Bentt ('A' High Jump), Bob Couillault ('B' Triple Jump) and the 4 x 100 metres relay team of Lee Sullivan, Bruno Hafner, Charlie Gillett and Steve White.

Steve White has wasted little time in making his impact on Iffley Road, having already won the Oxford Freshmen's 100m. and 200m., and represented Oxford in the Relays and Field Events matches with the other place.

Steve White is listed as 30th in the 200m., with several wind-assisted times above him, while John Thresher takes 43rd place in the 1,500m. For all our middle distance strength, we have no men in the 5,000 list, but Gerry North, in one of his few track runs, gained 27th place in the 10,000m.
As we have not heard how fit JIM VIVIAN is, I can only say that STEVE WHITE who is the most promising sprinter we have , will be our main runner this year - when he is not competing for Oxford.
This year's Surrey championships produced some good Belgrave performances, both from established stars like Steve White and up-and-coming men like Philip Gee.

Steve White played a major part in Oxford University's victory over Cambridge at the Crystal Palace on May 1. Although only fourth in the 100m. in 11.1s., Steve won the 200m. in 22.3s., and the long-jump, with a clearance of 23' 3½".

Top of the list were Steve White and Glyn Ratcliffe. Steve fairly set the cinders flying in the 200m., in which he equalled his personal best of 21.7s. to score a clear win; and he also took the long-jump.

Steve White has been going great guns in the long-jump this season, and it was no surprise when he cleared 24' 0¾" to win the event for a combined Oxford and Cambridge Universities team against Harvard and Yale at the Crystal Palace.
Steve White was Lambeth's star of the day, winning the 100m. in 10.8s. (wind assisted), and then took the long-jump, with a personal best (since improved) of 23' 4¾".
Also representing Surrey in the Motspur Park fixture was Steve White, who clocked 22.5s. for second in the 200m., and cleared 21' 6¾" for second in the long-jump.
Steve White has put up some good performances in university competitions, as can be seen from the results below, in which Mel Ford and John Bicourt also figure.

Steve White jumped 7.08m or 23ft 2¾ins but only managed seventh and Rodney Heward-Mills qualified for the final of the Triple Jump. An Inter-Club meeting at Chiswick on the last day of May saw the Bel's turn out in force in the 800m to show what depth we have in this event.

Result 1.Belgrave H. 67 pts 2.Hillingdon A.C. 56½ pts 3.Hercules/Wimbledon 53 pts 4.T.V.H. 52½ pts 5.Surrey A.C. 45½ pts 6.H.H.H. 44½ pts 7.Cambridge H. 35 pts 8.Borough of Enfield 14 pts 9.S.L.H. 11 pts 10.Croydon H. 8 pts 11.Blackheath H. 4 pts STEVE WHITE wins the "Brockman" long jump with a leap of 23'-2"

It cannot be said to have been a distinguished Southern Championships meeting for Belgrave, but John Bicourt produced some good form for third in the 3,000m. steeplechase, with a sub-nine minutes clocking, and Steve White was sixth in both the 200m. and the long-jump.
Our only winner in the "A" string events was Steve White, who scored an impressive victory in the 200m. - and also took part in the 100m., long-jump and both relays.

Steve White got a good hat-trick, in the 100m., 200m., and long-jump, however, while John Martin took the shot, discus, and (unlikely story) the high-jump with a personal best of 5' 2", and failed to add a fourth title, in the javelin, by just 2cm.

Steve White made a major contribution, with second places in the 200m. and in the long-jump, while Glyn Ratcliffe, as ever, was a tower of strength in the shot and discus, and Keith Schofield gave us a boost with a 56.90m./186' 8" javelin throw.
Steve White chalked up yet another sprint double, and Bill Kerr took the 1500m., while Jim Rimmer (3rd in 1m. 57.5s.) and John Boardman (fourth in 1m. 58s.) can be said to have run well in the 800m.

Steve White won the 200m., but suffered a rare reversal at the hands of a Club-mate, when junior Mick Marshall won the 100m. Mick - already a great asset - also took the junior long-jump, while Willie Williams made a jumping double in the junior events by clearing 1.52m. to win the high jump.

We did field a more competent team, but could not move higher than fifth position. Our only track winner of the day was none other than Steve White, in the "B" 100m. Steve also competed in the 200m. and both relays .
Best known are internationals Alan Lerwill, Britain's successor to Lynn Davies, and Derek Cole - both second claim Belgravians, and Belgravians John Mitchell and Steve White.
Steve White and Jim Vivian, who we were very pleased to see back on the track this year, both completed sprint doubles and Charlie Gillett won both the 400m hurdles and the 400m 'B' race.

John Bicourt's 5000m/1500m stint was a particularly good effort one feels but for sheer grace and power, the running and jumping of Steve White had no comparison, times not meaning a great deal in the windy conditions.

He was placed 3rd behind Yves Brouzet, the Frenchman who was 12th in Munich, and the German Jack Forst. Steve White won the 100 metres in 11.3 and the Long Jump in 6.92 metres. - photo by kind permission of Wimbledon News.
Rodney Heward-Mills gained our solitary medal with a 15.54 triple jump but Steve White only just missed in an exciting long jump competition in which 2 centimetres covered 2nd to 5th places.
Steve White and Mick Marshall had the 100m/200m pretty well sewn up, and Charlie and Phil. Gee were first past the post in both the long sprint races.

Finishing strongly, John Bicourt closed to about 10 metres by the finish for a clear 2nd and another world-class time. Steve White looked a bit tense in the 200 metre final but ran well in a field which included five internationals.

Steve White was in brilliant form, breaking the Southern League 200m record and equalling our own Club mark with 21.6. Unfortunately our sprinters suffered a set-back when Mick Marshall, after doing well in the 100m, TJ and LJ, "pulled" a hamstring in the 'B' 200m and had to step out of the relay squad.

After a bright start our lack of depth began to tell and despite great efforts from many people, especially Snowy Brooks, Charlie Gillett, Steve White and Arnold Bentt, we gradually slipped behind Mitcham and it looked as though we would have to settle for second place.

Steve White showed terrific winter form with 3rd place in the 100 metres final. He won his heat in 12.0 and then as there was quite a headwind they ran the final in the opposite direction and this time he clocked 11.1.
It is in the sprints, however, that we are at our most powerful, Steve White's flowing movement contrasting with Mick Marshall's power-house action but both with the same effect.
Superfast times came from Steve White in the 100th Oxford v Cambridge match on May 16th at West London, and it was nice to read in the paper next morning: "White is Oxford's hero".
Even our ever reliable Steve White was forced to accept a couple of second places, a most unusual occurrence, and this in spite of producing a noteworthy 10.9/21.9 .
Now representing Berkshire Steve White ran in the 100m heats (11.1) and was 6th in the 200m final (22.2). In the Long Jump Martin Scott (6.76) finished 10th for the North Eastern Counties.
His 49.7 for 2nd place in the 400m final seemed quite commonplace after that, inside the old County record as it was. It is obvious that Steve White's Junior Club mark of 49.4 is in danger.

Immediately, those connected with the track and field side could not help being impressed by the slim youngster who trained with purpose from the very beginning, who seemed to know exactly what he w…

Unfortunately space does not permit me to list them all but Steve White (who travels from Oxford to compete for the club) and Charlie Gillett deserve a mention for their efforts; neither ever seems to have a bad run.

This gave Steve White the chance to have a rest from the short events and tackle the one lap race for a change. The net result was the same as usual with Steve crossing the line first in a most comfortable looking 50.6 seconds.

Steve White, not jumping at his best, was 14th in the long jump with 6.75m whilst on the track Carl Lawton and John Hall distinguished themselves in the 3,000 metres Walk with 5th and 11th positions, both setting up new personal records.

Steve White led the way with another fine sprint double and later anchored both our relay teams. Cliff Brooks won his first ever pole vault competition and Philip Gee provided our only other points maximum in the 400 metres 'B'.
Two Belgravians competed; Steve White won the 200m in 22.5 and placed 2nd in the long jump with 6.84m, and M. Scammell clocked 14:44.2 to reach 2nd in the 3,000 metre walk.
Strangely enough many of our best individuals are also marvellous team members, particularly Steve White and the ever-reliable Cliff Brooks whose Decathlon points are still improving.

Steve White in the last "Spotlight" hit the nail right on the head with: "...unless there is some attempt to win the league and get into the National League one of the fundamental drives of athletics is denied - the will to win.".
At the A.G.M. last autumn LAURIE O'HARA and GEORGE PIDDINGTON were elected Life Members whilst BERNARD MERRY, STEVE WHITE and ALAN MEAD became Vice-Presidents.

A double win from Steve White and Steve Crosbie in the long jump, a personal best vault from Reg Hopkins and very good shot putting from John Martin set an impressive standard that if maintained throughout the year should stand us in good stead.

With Steve White and John Bicourt selected to compete at the British International Games on the same day our hopes took a tumble, and when sprinter Jim Evans became ill the day before the meeting all thoughts of winning had gone - it was to be a fight to avoid a real hammering.
Competing for the combined Oxford and Cambridge team against Harvard and Yale at Iffley Road, Oxford in June, Steve White again equalled his 200m club record of 21.6.

Steve White again picked up maximum score in each of his events and he was backed up by Jim Evans, equalling his 11.3 best again, and Martin Scott who does us great service by regularly turning out and cruising below his best with that nagging leg injury.

We certainly had the problems, for of our fifteen team members only two had not competed the previous day in the league, and after warming up for the 100 metres, Steve White, down for four events including relays, had to pull out with a knee problem.

Highlights included 22.9 for Charlie Gillett and 23.1 for Jim Evans over 200m, 49.8/400 Steve White, sub-50 from Steve and Charlie in the 4x400, 14:35.0/5000 from John Stow, 13.21/TJ from Steve Crosbie, 3.35/PV from Reg Hopkins ................................

Gerry's Club Record of 47.7 has been on the books since 1960 but as fast a time as this is, however, it does appear to be a mark which could be revised in the next couple of seasons when Vice President STEVE WHITE gets his teeth into one lap racing.
Steve White was still not completely recovered from his knee problem so rather than aggravate it with all out sprinting, he ran in the 400m and placed a close 2nd to Laing of SLH with 49.8.
Jim Evans won his 'B' 100m taking advantage of that same wind, clocking a personal best of 11.1, the same time as Steve White in the 'A' race.
Congratulations to JEAN and STEVE WHITE on the arrival of baby THOMAS. PETER NORTH has qualified for the gold award in the Duke of Edinburgh's Award Scheme - well done!
Steve White's 21.6 200m gained him =15th place and Glyn Ratcliffe was 20th in the discus (48.86). The only event in which two of our members made the top 50 was the decathlon.
Sadly we have had to say farewell - at least on a first claim basis - to Stephen White, the powerful sprinter who has supported us nobly for years in spite of living at Oxford.

He equalled his new Club 100m mark of 10.6 and also shaved a tenth off Steve White's 200m record with 21.5. He has not left things to rest there however, for in August in an Open Meeting at West London he cut that 100m time again - to 10.5.

From this period on Belgrave Harriers were fortunate in having a remarkable squad of long jumpers training under coach Dave Ansell's supervision: John Mitchell, Cliff Brooks, Bob Jones and later Alan Lerwill and Steve White.
The handicap was jointly won by the improving Youth John Gladwin and by Steve White, with Junior Mark Sinclair showing very good form to gain 3rd place.
